definition: Learning continuous embedding vectors prepended to the input (not human-readable text) while freezing the model.
details: Learning continuous embedding vectors prepended to the input (not human-readable text) while freezing the model. Extremely parameter-light; works best on large models and narrow tasks.

explainer.lead: A parameter-light method that learns continuous embedding vectors prepended to the input while the model's own weights stay frozen. It works best on large models and narrow tasks.

tiers.eli5: Instead of rewriting the instructions, you attach a small learned prefix of numbers to the input and let training find the prefix that works.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers freeze the model and train only the prefix vectors, which is cheap to store per task. A pitfall is expecting strong results on small models or broad tasks, where it tends to underperform.
tiers.paperLevel: Learn a continuous vector P prepended to input embeddings with the model frozen; extremely parameter-light, best on large models and narrow tasks.

explainer.example: For a sentiment task, a short learned prefix is trained once and reused, without updating any of the base model's parameters.
